title: Cascading Triggers: A Model Switch Followed by a Cache-Expiry

turns.userMessage: Let's refactor the notifications service to use an event bus.
turns.assistantResponse: Sure, looking at the notifications service now.
turns.explanation: Normal first turn under Model A — writes the static prefix plus this turn's own content.

turns.userMessage: Use an in-process event emitter for now, not a message queue.
turns.assistantResponse: Got it, using an in-process event emitter.
turns.explanation: Normal turn reusing/extending Model A's cache.

turns.userMessage: Switch to the more capable model — this refactor is getting complex.
turns.assistantResponse: Switching models now and continuing with the full context.
turns.explanation: Model switch: Model A's 4,100-token cache is worthless to Model B, so the whole history plus the new message is resent as uncached input, and Model B writes its own first cache entry from scratch at its own, pricier rates — identical mechanics to a standalone model-switch scenario.

turns.userMessage: Looks great — go ahead and start on the event bus interface. I'll be back in a bit.
turns.assistantResponse: Starting on the event bus interface now.
turns.explanation: Normal turn under Model B; cache builds up again. The user then steps away for over 5 minutes before the next turn — long enough to exceed Model B's default TTL too, on top of the model switch that already happened just two turns ago.

turns.userMessage: Ok I'm back — continue with the event bus interface.
turns.assistantResponse: Picking this back up — continuing with the event bus interface.
turns.explanation: Second invalidation in three turns, and it compounds: the idle gap exceeds Model B's TTL, so the entire 5,320-token history built up since the model switch is evicted and must be resent uncached — at Model B's pricier rates, since the earlier model switch never reverted. This turn (0.1242 AI Credits) is the most expensive in the session by far: it pays both the 'no warm cache' tax and the 'expensive model' tax at once. A single-trigger session (just a model switch, or just a TTL lapse) never stacks costs this way — cascading triggers are worse than the sum of either alone would suggest, because each subsequent trigger keeps re-paying the pricier post-switch rates.

turns.assistantResponse: Sounds good — the event bus interface is in place.
turns.explanation: Cache finally recovers to normal healthy growth — but only after paying for both cascading triggers earlier in the session. Total session AI Credits here run well above either a model-switch-only scenario (about 0.176 AI Credits total via a comparable arc) or a TTL-lapse-only scenario (about 0.167 AI Credits total) alone, because this session paid both taxes back to back.
